one_liner: Senior Executive Service leader running the Forest Service's national wildland fire workforce, employee well-being, budget, procurement, and data systems programs from DC.
fit_summary: This is a career SES role that requires proven executive-level leadership of large organizations, budgets, and people, plus wildland fire management expertise (TQ1). Daniel's emergency-management consulting background at IEM and strong policy knowledge are relevant, but nothing on file shows executive-level supervision or wildland fire operations. A QRB is unlikely to certify that background against the ECQs.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths: fed-competitive, ses, public), so no federal status is needed to apply.
Your resume alone must demonstrate all five ECQs and both TQs, including wildland fire management and dealing with Congress and the media. Applicants who don't show them are ruled ineligible.
Selectees must be certified by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board before appointment, then serve a one-year probationary period.
A Top Secret clearance is listed. It is likely obtained after selection, but you must be able to pass a background investigation.
strategy: Be realistic. Unless your IEM work included directing large teams or multimillion-dollar programs, use this posting to learn what SES boards expect rather than as a primary target.
If you apply, keep to the strict 2-page limit (0.8-inch margins, 11-point font) and label your accomplishments by ECQ. Do not submit separate ECQ or TQ narratives.
Frame your IEM experience around government-client disaster recovery and preparedness programs. Quantify any budgets, staff, jurisdictions, or federal funds you managed, using only true figures.
Use your policy and relationship strengths for ECQ1 (Knowledge of the American System of Government) and TQ2 (Congress, media, officials). Give concrete examples of stakeholder engagement.

Apply between Oct 16 and Nov 6, 2026, and complete the USA Staffing questionnaire. In parallel, target GS-11/12/13 FEMA, emergency management, or program analyst roles and Virginia or NoVA emergency management jobs where you're competitive.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] disaster recovery program totaling [$ amount], coordinating [number] federal, state, and local stakeholders to [specific outcome].
Led [team size] staff on [preparedness/recovery project], improving [process/metric] by [result] through [technology or process upgrade].
Briefed [senior officials/elected officials/media] on [policy issue], resulting in [decision or outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a large, geographically distributed organization through change and held people accountable.
How have you cut wasteful spending or improved efficiency in a budget you controlled?
How would you represent the Forest Service's wildland fire priorities before Congress and the media?
What experience do you have with wildland fire operations or policy?
watch_outs: SES level: the QRB requires demonstrated executive experience, which your record likely doesn't yet show.
TQ1 requires wildland fire management expertise that isn't in your background.
A Top Secret clearance is required, and the position is based onsite in DC with telework eligibility, not remote.
Resumes longer than 2 pages may be disqualified.
